To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chimeric and beta template peptide constructs of human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 surface envelope peptides with promiscuous peptides are more immunogenic than their linear forms and overcome genetic restriction of immune responses.
the use of chimeric and beta template peptides in combination with a promiscuous T cell epitope enhances the immunogenicity of the retroviral peptide.

chimeric peptide constructs of the human T-lymphotropic virus type 1 gp46 protein containing promiscuous helper T-cell epitopes are highly immunogenic and elicit antibodies that recognize the native form of the viral envelope protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of immunogenic constructs of retroviral peptides that are effective in overcoming genetic restriction of the immune response to synthetic peptide vaccines and that can be used to elicit protective antibody and T-cell responses.
the development of a vaccine to prevent human retroviral infections and to control disease progression in HTLV-1 carriers.
the design and evaluation of immunogens for HTLV-1 infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

promiscuous peptides, such as those derived from tetanus toxin and measles virus, may be used to overcome the problem of genetically restricted immune responses and enhance the immune response to synthetic peptides.

the use of multivalent and chimeric constructs incorporating promiscuous T-helper epitopes may be useful for overcoming genetically restricted immune reactivity to retroviral epitopes and may have broad application in the design of vaccines against other retroviruses and other infectious agents.

chimeric and beta- template peptide constructs incorporating known HTLV-1 B- and T- cell epitopes and promiscuous peptides were highly immunogenic and elicited elevated antibody titers and lymphoproliferative responses in each strain of mice tested, including those of diverse major histocmpatibility complex haplotypes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach for overcoming genetic restriction to immunization with retroviral peptides.
we have demonstrated that the use of promis-cuous T-cell epitope chimeric constructs can be used to overcome the genetically restricted responses to retroviral synthetic peptides.

the use of promisuous T-cell epitope chimeric constructs can enhance the immunogenicity of viral peptides, overcome MHC restriction, and promote the development of virus-specific T-cell and B-cell responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunogenicity of viral peptide vaccines can be enhanced by the use of multivalent constructs that include known viral epitopes with promiscuous helper T-cell peptides.
promiscuous T cell epitope constructs can be used to enhance the immunogenicity of viral peptide constructs and overcome genetically restricted immune responses.
chimeric constructs are more immunogenic than the native peptide, and the immunogenicity of the chimeric construct is not limited to the mouse strains tested.
